summary: Iteration 160 — Internal Data AI fuel/activity consumption routing fix. Verified planner routing (26 unit tests) + new integration tests (6) covering analytics.query() fuel_type propagation, consumption_breakdown response field, emissions.search_records() fuel_type filter, and live backend reachability (login + /api/internal-ai/chat). All 32 tests PASS. Live logs confirm 'How much Crude Oil was consumed for July 2026?' now routes to emissions.search_records with fuel_type='Crude Oil' — no longer to esg_records.get_kpis. The 'No data found' answer in the live env is a legitimate empty-result response (no matching Crude Oil emission records for July 2026), not a routing bug.
critical_code_review_comments: analytics.py:113 — consumption_breakdown builder does c['_id'].get(...) which assumes _id is always a dict. If a legacy emission_record row has fuel_type=None AND unit=None, Mongo will still return a dict with None values (safe). But if the $group stage were ever changed to a scalar _id, this would raise AttributeError. Consider a defensive isinstance(c['_id'], dict) guard.

planner.py:98 — kpi_lookup falls through to esg_records.get_kpis only when is_emission_metric is False. Because 'consumed' / 'consumption' keywords force is_emission_metric=True, any KPI whose metric name happens to contain 'consumption' (e.g. 'water consumption per employee', which IS a legitimate KPI) will be misrouted to analytics.query. Consider a small allow-list of KPI names that must always hit the metadata catalog even when the string contains 'consumption'.

The intent detector currently classifies 'How much Crude Oil was consumed…' as record_lookup (not kpi_lookup) in the live env. The fix still works because record_lookup with record_type='emission' also routes to emissions.search_records with fuel_type. Both paths are now safe — worth documenting so future refactors don't regress one of them.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 160 fuel-routing fix is fully verified. Planner unit tests are at /app/backend/tests/test_internal_ai_fuel_routing_iter160.py (26 tests). New integration tests at /app/backend/tests/test_internal_ai_fuel_integration_iter160.py (6 tests) use a fake Motor collection to assert fuel_type propagates into aggregate() pipelines and find() queries. Live-endpoint tests hit /api/auth/login and /api/internal-ai/chat with real admin creds. When testing next changes to internal_data_ai, run both files together: pytest tests/test_internal_ai_fuel_routing_iter160.py tests/test_internal_ai_fuel_integration_iter160.py -v.
rca of the issue: Original bug: kpi_lookup intent unconditionally routed to esg_records.get_kpis (the KPI-definition metadata catalog). The is_emission_metric heuristic only checked record_type=='emission' or 'emission'/'ghg' substrings in the metric name — it missed the case where the LLM extracted fuel_type='Crude Oil' but left record_type/metric ambiguous. Fix (verified): planner.py adds _has_operational_data_dimension(entities) which flags any non-null fuel_type/scope/category/facility as an operational-data query. When True + fuel_type present → emissions.search_records. When True + no fuel_type → analytics.query. When False → esg_records.get_kpis (genuine KPI). analytics.py additionally accepts fuel_type kwarg, injects a $regex match into every aggregate pipeline, and returns a new consumption_breakdown array (grouped by fuel_type + unit with total_quantity and total_emissions). Live logs at 2026-08-10 12:29 confirm end-to-end plumbing works.
